configuration.identical_across_orders: fixture, frame count, working scale, NVOF grid and preset, DLSS options, depth convention, encoder, CQ and output resolution; only transfer_mode differs
configuration.schedule_rule: odd executions launch legacy first, even executions reduced first, and the kept pairs alternate, so the kept pairs of one execution contain one pair of each position

output_integrity_gate.what: legacy run 1 ffprobe reports a complete stream
legacy run 2 ffprobe reports a complete stream
legacy run 3 ffprobe reports a complete stream
reduced run 1 ffprobe reports a complete stream
reduced run 2 ffprobe reports a complete stream
reduced run 3 ffprobe reports a complete stream
run 1 video bitstream bit-identical between orders
run 2 video bitstream bit-identical between orders
run 3 video bitstream bit-identical between orders

measurement_rules.counters: median over the frames after the first of each kept run, then median across those runs; the reset frame uploads twice and is excluded
measurement_rules.fps: frames recorded divided by the wall clock of export_dlss_stream() alone, the same window tests/unit/benchmark_e2e.py times, so the figures can be read against the recorded 5.164 and 7.247 FPS baselines. Session creation happens before the window opens and is not in either number.
measurement_rules.spans: p50 and p95 of every frame record of the kept runs, in ms
measurement_rules.unavailable: None means the run did not measure it; 0 means it measured zero
measurement_rules.warmup: the warmup pairs are run and published with included_in_medians=false; no median, ratio, pair or sign test here or downstream reads them

output_identity.note: Matroska writes a random SegmentUID and a per-run timestamp into every file, so no two exports of this pipeline hash alike, two runs of the same order included. The numbers above are measured: the count of differing bytes and their position relative to the first Cluster, which is where the payload starts. A container hash is therefore reported here as a diagnostic and the gate compares the bitstream.
